title: Scalar FlashBridge: lane-aware prefetch scheduler and KV warmup microkernel
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production workloads with mixed sequence lengths still pay tail latency due to cold KV hotspots and coarse-grained prefetch. This PR introduces a scalarized variant of the FlashBridge attention path that exposes lane-level prefetch hints to the scheduler and a tiny KV warmup microkernel that runs asynchronously during continuous batching backpressure periods. High-level changes: 1) scalar flashbridge attn microkernel: a smaller, less-register-hungry kernel optimized for narrow lanes and short sequences; falls back to existing fused kernel for wide lanes. 2) lane-aware prefetch scheduler: scheduler tracks per-lane sequence distribution and issues targeted prefetch requests (rotary offsets + KV pages) prioritized by predicted hot paths. 3) async KV warmup microkernel: non-blocking warmup thread launches prioritized KV loads using a lightweight coalescer to avoid blocking the main inference path. 4) continuous-batching backpressure integration: when batcher detects a temporary overload, it pushes low-priority warmup jobs instead of dropping requests; this improves warm cache hit-rate under bursty load. 5) telemetry and safety: new latency buckets, a warmup hit/miss gauge, and toggles for max warmup concurrency. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-1928) - [x] microkernel implemented and unit-tested - [x] scheduler integration with existing resource hints - [x] end-to-end nightly benchmark added - [x] doc comment blocks and API knobs exposed - [x] toggles gated behind runtime flags for canary rollout Compatibility notes: feature is opt-in via runtime flag `scalar_flashbridge_enabled`; default remains current fused path. Rollout plan: canary on Dedicated staging pool -> gradual ramp using rollout policy (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) with perf regression guardrails. Benchmarks: end-to-end p50 latency improved 6-9% for short sequences (<128 tokens) and p95 improved 12-18% for mixed workloads; throughput increased by 8% for 4-8 token sequences under high concurrency due to reduced KV stalls. Memory overhead: warmup buffer adds ~2%-4% VRAM on GPUs with aggressive warmup enabled. Risks and mitigations: - incorrect prefetch ordering can increase pressure on PCIe; mitigated by token-budgeted prefetch rate limiter - warmup thrashing on extremely bursty input distributions; mitigated by per-customer warmup caps and adaptive decay. Related: builds on prior FlashBridge and prefetched rotary work, but uses a scalar kernel path to reduce register pressure on Ampere/Grace architectures and to better handle narrow-lane scheduling.
